mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% signals monetary tightening, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%), or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises concurrently with an increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE > 0.3pp in 3 months), it signals a tightening policy amid economic weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2pp in 1 month AND UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rise as specified, or the interaction term's coefficient is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a regression model.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of sustained GDP growth (GDPC1 quarterly growth > 1.5%), corporate earnings prospects improve, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
regime_hint: strong GDP growth regime (GDPC1 quarterly growth > 1.5%)
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 1.5%, or the regime-specific Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.5%) indicates a tight labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate profits, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 (INDPRO < 100) signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, reducing corporate earnings expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances (INDPRO < 100), or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market expansion (HOUST > 1200 thousand units), increased construction activity and consumer confidence boost economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST exceeds 1200, or the regime-specific Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST > 1200) coincide with weak industrial production (INDPRO < 100), it indicates a sectoral imbalance where demand is strong but supply is constrained, leading to inflationary pressures and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: sectoral imbalance (housing boom with industrial contraction)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where HOUST > 1200 and INDPRO < 100, or the interaction term's coefficient is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a regression model.
